Now the fundamental theorem and subtype soundness. Let's spell out the FT statement:

Definition env_ok (rho) (sigma) (RGamma) :=
  forall x R, lookup_rcontext x RGamma = Some R -> ET (rty_env rho sigma R) (sigma x).

Theorem fundamental_has_rtype: forall Delta RGamma t R, has_rtype Delta RGamma t R ->
  forall rho sigma, (forall X, locally_closed_ty (rho X)) -> (forall x, locally_closed_tm (sigma x)) ->
  env_ok rho sigma RGamma ->
  ET (rty_env rho sigma R) (tm_env rho sigma t).

And subtype soundness:
Theorem subtype_sound: forall Delta RGamma R S, subtype Delta RGamma R S ->
  forall rho sigma, ... -> env_ok ... ->
  (forall v, VT (rty_env rho sigma R) v -> VT (rty_env rho sigma S) v) /\
  (forall t, ET (rty_env rho sigma R) t -> ET (rty_env rho sigma S) t).

Given w ∈ VT[[S1]], need ET[[R_Exists S1 S2]] (app v w) = exists w', VT[[S1]] w' /\ ET[[open S2 w']] (app v w). Take w' = w: need VT[[S1]] w ✓ and ET[[open S2 w]] (app v w). We need to prove:
(FT) forall Delta RGamma t R, has_rtype Delta RGamma t R -> forall rho sigma, Hrho -> Hsigma -> env_ok rho sigma RGamma -> ET (rty_env rho sigma R) (close_tm rho sigma t).
(ST) forall Delta RGamma R S, subtype Delta RGamma R S -> forall rho sigma, Hrho -> Hsigma -> env_ok rho sigma RGamma -> (forall v, VT (rty_env rho sigma R) v -> VT (rty_env rho sigma S) v) /\ (forall t, ET (rty_env rho sigma R) t -> ET (rty_env rho sigma S) t).

Mutual induction on the has_rtype/subtype derivation. In Coq, use the Scheme-generated mutual induction, or `induction d using has_rtype_mut`. But the statement has the environment quantifiers. Let me think about the practical Rocq mechanics.

We can define:
Definition FT_stmt (d : has_rtype Delta RGamma t R) : Prop := forall rho sigma, Hrho rho -> Hsigma sigma -> env_ok rho sigma RGamma -> ET (rty_env rho sigma R) (close_tm rho sigma t).
But Delta,RGamma,t,R are implicit in d; in Coq, `has_rtype Delta RGamma t R` with indices; a function over the proof requires the indices be parameters: Definition FT_stmt (Delta RGamma t R) (d : has_rtype Delta RGamma t R) := ... . That's fine.

Similarly ST_stmt.

Then: Scheme has_rtype_mut := Induction for has_rtype Sort Prop with subtype_mut := Induction for subtype Sort Prop.

Then apply has_rtype_mut with (P := FT_stmt) (Q := ST_stmt). Each rule case becomes a goal where we assume the rule premises and IHs (for recursive premises of the same relation) plus Q hypotheses (for subtype premises) and must prove FT_stmt of the conclusion. Note: the induction principle provides the IH for *recursive premises* of has_rtype only; for subtype premises in has_rtype rules (RT_Sub), it provides the Q property, but Q's statement at the premise's indices is exactly ST_stmt for that subtype derivation ✓. But Q itself is fixed as ST_stmt? In the Scheme, Q is a variable predicate over subtype derivations: Q := fun Delta RGamma R S (d : subtype ...) => ...; the mutual induction gives the Q hypothesis for subtype premises assuming we've proven all the subtype cases. Yes.

But note: ST's statement quantifies over rho sigma and env_ok; when used in RT_Sub's case, the premise gives exactly that ✓.

However, in RWF_* etc. (wf_rty), no mutual induction needed (has_rtype's rules mention wf_rty which references qualifier_wf/has_type, not has_rtype/subtype).

In S_Witness, the premise has_rtype Delta RGamma v R1 is an *has_rtype* premise inside a subtype rule. The mutual induction principle for subtype provides, for has_rtype premises, the P property (P := FT_stmt) ✓. Great.

So the mutual induction handles the circularity.

One concern: does Coq's combined Scheme handle rules where the recursive occurrence is under a forall (e.g., RT_Abs's premise forall x, ... has_rtype ...)? Yes, the IH will be for all x.

Another concern: the induction principle's P and Q are over the *indices*, so P : forall Delta RGamma t R, has_rtype Delta RGamma t R -> Prop; when applying has_rtype_mut, Coq will instantiate P and Q; we need to provide proofs of each rule's case with P/Q. The generated case types can be inspected with `Show` or `Set Printing`. We'll iterate.

Now the semantic definitions in detail. Let me write them.

Inductive CV : ty -> tm -> Prop := ... Since CV has no recursion, define as a Fixpoint returning Prop:
Definition CV (T : ty) (v : tm) : Prop :=
  match T with
  | Ty_BVar _ => True
  | Ty_FVar _ => True
  | Ty_Int => exists n, v = tm_int n
  | Ty_Arrow _ _ => exists T0 body, v = tm_abs T0 body
  | Ty_All _ => exists body, v = tm_tabs body
  end.

Hmm, for Ty_Arrow, should we require locally_closed? value v already includes lc for abs. Fine.

Now ET/VT mutual inductive. Let me define:

Inductive ET : rty -> tm -> Prop :=
| ET_intro : forall R t v, locally_closed_tm t -> multi t v -> VT R v -> ET R t.

with VT : rty -> tm -> Prop :=
| VT_Refine : forall T ps v, value v -> CV T v -> qualifier_holds (open_qualifier_tm ps v) -> VT (R_Refine T ps) v
| VT_Func : forall R1 R2 v, value v -> (forall w, VT R1 w -> ET (R_Exists R1 R2) (tm_app v w)) -> VT (R_Func R1 R2) v
| VT_Exists : forall R1 R2 v, value v -> (exists w, ET R1 w /\ ET (open_rty_tm R2 w) v) -> VT (R_Exists R1 R2) v
| VT_Poly : forall R v, value v -> (exists body, v = tm_tabs body /\ forall U, locally_closed_ty U -> ET (open_rty_ty R U) (open_tm_ty body U)) -> VT (R_Poly R) v.

Note: VT is defined by the mutual block; its clauses mention ET.

Now let's think about the mutual induction mechanics more concretely, especially the cases with premises that are has_rtype/subtype under binders.

The generated induction principle has for each rule a case; e.g., for RT_Abs:
forall (L : list atom) Delta RGamma R1 body R2,
  wf_rty Delta RGamma R1 ->
  (forall x, ~ In x L -> has_rtype Delta (update_rcontext RGamma x R1) (open_tm body (fvar x)) (open_rty_tm R2 (fvar x))) ->
  (forall x, ~ In x L -> P Delta (update_rcontext RGamma x R1) (open_tm body (fvar x)) (open_rty_tm R2 (fvar x)) (premise_x)) ->  (* IH *)
  P Delta RGamma (tm_abs (erase R1) body) (R_Func R1 R2)
where P is FT_stmt. Note the IH requires the derivation premise as an argument; in the Scheme-generated principle, the IH is typically of the form `(forall x H, P ... (d x H))` where d is the premise function. When we apply the induction principle, we need to handle this. Since the premise is a function (forall x, ~ In x L -> has_rtype ...), the induction principle provides the IH as `forall x Hx, P ... (premise x Hx)`. Good.

For rules with multiple has_rtype premises (RT_App, RT_Div...), we get separate IHs.

For subtype rules with has_rtype premises (S_Witness), the subtype's mutual induction gives P for the has_rtype premise.

Now the proof of each case will be a lemma statement with all parameters universally quantified. Practical approach in Rocq: prove the theorem using the induction principle and then `intros` in each goal. This is going to be long but straightforward-ish.

Alternatively, avoid Scheme and prove everything by induction on a *combined derivation size*? Scheme is easier.

Let me now also think about whether env_ok should be defined with ET or VT. RT_Var's goal is ET (rty_env R) (sigma x). If env_ok uses ET, great. In S_Bind's use we need ET R1' w ✓. In S_Refine's extension we need ET (R_Refine T' True) v ✓ (can build from VT). So env_ok with ET.

env_ok definition: Definition env_ok (rho sigma : ...) (RGamma : rcontext) : Prop := forall x R, lookup_rcontext x RGamma = Some R -> ET (rty_env rho sigma R) (sigma x).

But in RT_Abs, the term in the conclusion is tm_abs (erase R1) body, whose close_tm = tm_abs (ty_env rho (erase R1)) (close_tm rho sigma body) ✓ definitional. The rty_env (R_Func R1 R2) = R_Func (rty_env R1) (rty_env R2) ✓ definitional.

Now let's think about the commutation lemmas for close_tm/open_tm etc. precisely and their hypotheses.

Definitions:

Fixpoint ty_env (rho : atom -> ty) (T : ty) : ty :=
  match T with
  | Ty_BVar i => Ty_BVar i
  | Ty_FVar X => rho X
  | Ty_Arrow T1 T2 => Ty_Arrow (ty_env rho T1) (ty_env rho T2)
  | Ty_All T1 => Ty_All (ty_env rho T1)
  | Ty_Int => Ty_Int
  end.

Fixpoint tm_env (rho : atom -> ty) (sigma : atom -> tm) (t : tm) : tm := ...
  | tm_fvar x => sigma x
  | tm_abs T t1 => tm_abs (ty_env rho T) (tm_env rho sigma t1)
  | tm_tapp t1 T => tm_tapp (tm_env rho sigma t1) (ty_env rho T)
  ...

Fixpoint qual_env (rho sigma) (q : qualifier) : qualifier :=
  | Pred_Eq t1 t2 => Pred_Eq (tm_env rho sigma t1) (tm_env rho sigma t2)
  ...

Fixpoint rty_env rho sigma R :=
  | R_Refine T ps => R_Refine (ty_env rho T) (qual_env rho sigma ps)
  | R_Func R1 R2 => R_Func (rty_env R1) (rty_env R2)
  | R_Exists R1 R2 => R_Exists (rty_env R1) (rty_env R2)
  | R_Poly R => R_Poly (rty_env R)
  end.

Note: rty_env does NOT do anything binder-aware: it just substitutes fvars everywhere, which is correct since fvars are never bound by rty binders (binders are bvars) ✓.

Commutation lemmas:

  | R_Refine T ps => fv_qual ps  (* T's ty has no term fvars *)
  | R_Func R1 R2 | R_Exists R1 R2 => fv_rty R1 ++ fv_rty R2

  | R_Func R1 R2 | R_Exists R1 R2 => ftv_rty R1 ++ ftv_rty R2

Let me write Stage 1.

```coq
Module SystemFRefinementSemantics.
Import ListNotations SystemFRefinement SystemFRefinementLogic SystemFRefinementTyping SystemFRefinementEvaluation.

(* ---------- Freshness utilities ---------- *)
Lemma max_atom_ge : forall L x, In x L -> x <= max_atom L.
Proof.
  induction L as [|a L IH]; intros x Hin; simpl in *.
  - inversion Hin.
  - destruct Hin as [-> | Hin].
    + apply Nat.le_max_l.
    + eapply Nat.le_trans; [apply IH, Hin | apply Nat.le_max_r].
Qed.

Lemma fresh_not_in : forall L, ~ In (fresh L) L.
Proof.
  intros L Hin. unfold fresh.
  pose proof max_atom_ge L _ Hin. lia.
Qed.
```

Then env definitions:

```coq
Fixpoint ty_env (rho : atom -> ty) (T : ty) : ty :=
  match T with
  | Ty_BVar i => Ty_BVar i
  | Ty_FVar X => rho X
  | Ty_Arrow T1 T2 => Ty_Arrow (ty_env rho T1) (ty_env rho T2)
  | Ty_All T1 => Ty_All (ty_env rho T1)
  | Ty_Int => Ty_Int
  end.

Fixpoint tm_env (rho : atom -> ty) (sigma : atom -> tm) (t : tm) : tm :=
  match t with
  | tm_bvar i => tm_bvar i
  | tm_fvar x => sigma x
  | tm_abs T t1 => tm_abs (ty_env rho T) (tm_env rho sigma t1)
  | tm_app t1 t2 => tm_app (tm_env rho sigma t1) (tm_env rho sigma t2)
  | tm_tabs t1 => tm_tabs (tm_env rho sigma t1)
  | tm_tapp t1 T => tm_tapp (tm_env rho sigma t1) (ty_env rho T)
  | tm_int n => tm_int n
  | tm_div t1 t2 => tm_div (tm_env rho sigma t1) (tm_env rho sigma t2)
  | tm_arith op t1 t2 => tm_arith op (tm_env rho sigma t1) (tm_env rho sigma t2)
  end.

Fixpoint qual_env (rho : atom -> ty) (sigma : atom -> tm) (q : qualifier) : qualifier :=
  match q with
  | Pred_True => Pred_True
  | Pred_False => Pred_False
  | Pred_Eq t1 t2 => Pred_Eq (tm_env rho sigma t1) (tm_env rho sigma t2)
  | Pred_Lt t1 t2 => Pred_Lt (tm_env rho sigma t1) (tm_env rho sigma t2)
  | Pred_Le t1 t2 => Pred_Le (tm_env rho sigma t1) (tm_env rho sigma t2)
  | Pred_And p1 p2 => Pred_And (qual_env rho sigma p1) (qual_env rho sigma p2)
  | Pred_Or p1 p2 => Pred_Or (qual_env rho sigma p1) (qual_env rho sigma p2)
  | Pred_Not p1 => Pred_Not (qual_env rho sigma p1)
  end.

Fixpoint rty_env (rho : atom -> ty) (sigma : atom -> tm) (R : rty) : rty :=
  match R with
  | R_Refine T ps => R_Refine (ty_env rho T) (qual_env rho sigma ps)
  | R_Func R1 R2 => R_Func (rty_env rho sigma R1) (rty_env rho sigma R2)
  | R_Exists R1 R2 => R_Exists (rty_env rho sigma R1) (rty_env rho sigma R2)
  | R_Poly R1 => R_Poly (rty_env rho sigma R1)
  end.
```

```coq
Module SystemFRefinementSemantics.
Import ListNotations SystemFRefinement SystemFRefinementLogic SystemFRefinementTyping SystemFRefinementEvaluation.

(* ---------- Freshness ---------- *)
Lemma max_atom_ge : forall (L : list atom) (x : atom), In x L -> x <= max_atom L.
Proof.
  induction L as [| a L IH]; intros x Hin; simpl in *.
  - inversion Hin.
  - destruct Hin as [-> | Hin].
    + apply Nat.le_max_l.
    + eapply Nat.le_trans; [apply IH; eassumption | apply Nat.le_max_r].
Qed.

Lemma fresh_not_in : forall (L : list atom), ~ In (fresh L) L.
Proof.
  intros L Hin. unfold fresh.
  pose proof max_atom_ge L _ Hin. lia.
Qed.

Definition upd_tm (x : atom) (w : tm) (sigma : atom -> tm) : atom -> tm :=
  fun y => if Nat.eqb y x then w else sigma y.

Definition upd_ty (X : atom) (U : ty) (rho : atom -> ty) : atom -> ty :=
  fun Y => if Nat.eqb Y X then U else rho Y.

Lemma upd_tm_eq : forall x w sigma, upd_tm x w sigma x = w.
Proof. intros. unfold upd_tm. rewrite Nat.eqb_refl. reflexivity. Qed.

Lemma upd_tm_neq : forall x y w sigma, x <> y -> upd_tm x w sigma y = sigma y.
Proof. intros. unfold upd_tm. destruct (Nat.eqb y x) eqn:E; [apply Nat.eqb_eq in E; congruence | reflexivity]. Qed.

Lemma upd_ty_eq : forall X U rho, upd_ty X U rho X = U.
Proof. intros. unfold upd_ty. rewrite Nat.eqb_refl. reflexivity. Qed.

Lemma upd_ty_neq : forall X Y U rho, X <> Y -> upd_ty X U rho Y = rho Y.
Proof. intros. unfold upd_ty. destruct (Nat.eqb Y X) eqn:E; [apply Nat.eqb_eq in E; congruence | reflexivity]. Qed.
```

  induction L as [| a L IH]; intros x Hin; simpl in *.
  - inversion Hin.
  - destruct Hin as [-> | Hin].
    + apply Nat.le_max_l.
    + eapply Nat.le_trans; [apply IH; eassumption | apply Nat.le_max_r].
Qed.

  intros L Hin. unfold fresh.

Definition upd_tm (x : atom) (w : tm) (sigma : atom -> tm) : atom -> tm :=
  fun y => if Nat.eqb y x then w else sigma y.

  fun Y => if Nat.eqb Y X then U else rho Y.

Definition CV (T : ty) (v : tm) : Prop :=
  match T with
  | Ty_BVar _ => True
  | Ty_FVar _ => True
  | Ty_Int => exists n : Z, v = tm_int n
  | Ty_Arrow _ _ => exists (T0 : ty) (body : tm), v = tm_abs T0 body
  | Ty_All _ => exists body : tm, v = tm_tabs body
  end.

Mutual inductive ET/VT:

Inductive ET : rty -> tm -> Prop :=
| ET_intro : forall R t v, locally_closed_tm t -> multi t v -> VT R v -> ET R t
with VT : rty -> tm -> Prop :=
| VT_Refine : forall T ps v, value v -> CV T v -> qualifier_holds (open_qualifier_tm ps v) -> VT (R_Refine T ps) v
| VT_Func : forall R1 R2 v, value v -> (forall w, VT R1 w -> ET (R_Exists R1 R2) (tm_app v w)) -> VT (R_Func R1 R2) v
| VT_Exists : forall R1 R2 v, value v -> (exists w, ET R1 w /\ ET (open_rty_tm R2 w) v) -> VT (R_Exists R1 R2) v
| VT_Poly : forall R v, value v -> (exists body, v = tm_tabs body /\ forall U, locally_closed_ty U -> ET (open_rty_ty R U) (open_tm_ty body U)) -> VT (R_Poly R) v.

Coq mutual inductive syntax:

with VT : rty -> tm -> Prop :=
  ...
.

Module SystemFRefinementLogicalRelation.
Import ListNotations SystemFRefinement SystemFRefinementLogic SystemFRefinementTyping SystemFRefinementEvaluation SystemFRefinementSemantics.

Definition CV (T : ty) (v : tm) : Prop :=
  match T with
  | Ty_BVar _ => True
  | Ty_FVar _ => True
  | Ty_Int => exists n : Z, v = tm_int n
  | Ty_Arrow _ _ => exists (T0 : ty) (body : tm), v = tm_abs T0 body
  | Ty_All _ => exists body : tm, v = tm_tabs body
  end.

Inductive ET : rty -> tm -> Prop :=
  | ET_intro : forall R t v,
      locally_closed_tm t ->
      multi t v ->
      VT R v ->
      ET R t
with VT : rty -> tm -> Prop :=
  | VT_Refine : forall T ps v,
      value v ->
      CV T v ->
      qualifier_holds (open_qualifier_tm ps v) ->
      VT (R_Refine T ps) v
  | VT_Func : forall R1 R2 v,
      value v ->
      (forall w, VT R1 w -> ET (R_Exists R1 R2) (tm_app v w)) ->
      VT (R_Func R1 R2) v
  | VT_Exists : forall R1 R2 v,
      value v ->
      (exists w, ET R1 w /\ ET (open_rty_tm R2 w) v) ->
      VT (R_Exists R1 R2) v
  | VT_Poly : forall R v,
      value v ->
      (exists body, v = tm_tabs body /\
         forall U, locally_closed_ty U -> ET (open_rty_ty R U) (open_tm_ty body U)) ->
      VT (R_Poly R) v.

Note the order: ET is defined first, referencing VT; Coq requires that the mutual block's constructors only refer to the block members. Fine.

  end
with ...

| R_Poly R => value v /\ exists body, v = tabs body /\ forall U, ET (ty_env?) ... R U ...  -- type binders!

The type binders: R_Poly R's bvar 0 is a *type* variable, not a term variable! Conflict: rty bvars are used for both term binders (R_Func/R_Exists/R_Refine) and type binders (R_Poly). open_rty_tm vs open_rty_ty distinguish them by which constructor increments. So the environment must be typed by binder kind: a single de Bruijn index space where R_Poly binds a type variable and R_Func/R_Exists bind term variables; the operations open_rty_tm/open_rty_ty increment their respective counts; the indices interact! E.g., R_Poly (R_Func R1 R2): the R_Func's R2's bvar 0 is the term arg, bvar 1 is the type variable. So the environment must map indices to either terms or types depending on the binder kind in scope. We can define the environment as a function nat -> tm (for term binders) plus nat -> ty (for type binders)? But the same index space is shared with different increments per binder type — the ordering of binders determines what each index means. Since open_rty_tm increments k at R_Func/R_Exists/R_Refine and open_rty_ty increments k at R_Poly, the indices count the total number of enclosing rty binders (both kinds). So an environment must know, for each binder index, whether it's a term or type binder. We'd need a list of binder kinds and a lookup.

So:
Fixpoint V (envT : list ty) (envM : list tm) (R : rty) (v : tm) {struct R} : Prop :=
  match R with
  | R_Refine T ps =>
      value v /\ CV (subst_ty_list envT T) v /\ qualifier_holds (subst_qual_list envT envM v ps)
  | R_Func R1 R2 =>
      value v /\ forall w, V envT envM R1 w ->
        (locally_closed_tm (tm_app v w) /\
         exists u, multi (tm_app v w) u /\ V envT (w :: envM) R2 u)
  | R_Exists R1 R2 =>
      value v /\ exists w,
        (locally_closed_tm w /\ exists u, multi w u /\ V envT envM R1 u) /\
        (locally_closed_tm v /\ exists u, multi v u /\ V envT (w :: envM) R2 u)
  | R_Poly R1 =>
      value v /\ exists body, v = tm_tabs body /\
        forall U, locally_closed_ty U ->
          (locally_closed_tm (open_tm_ty body U) /\
           exists u, multi (open_tm_ty body U) u /\ V (U :: envT) envM R1 u)
  end.

Standard approach for ty substitution with a *list* environment: define a function that substitutes free bvars using an environment, treating Ty_All binders by extending the environment with the bound variable represented as a shifted-up variable. Fixpoint subst_ty_list (env : list ty) (T : ty) : ty :=

This is where shifting of env entries matters: going under Ty_All, the free variables in the environment must be shifted by 1 because bvar indices inside are +1. The standard trick: env entries are represented as "terms in the outer context"; going under a binder requires *lifting* each entry by 1 (shift all free bvars by 1) and prepending the bound variable (represented by Ty_BVar 0).

So define:
Fixpoint lift_ty (T : ty) : ty := (* shift all free bvars by 1 *)
  match T with
  | Ty_BVar i => Ty_BVar (S i)
  | Ty_FVar X => Ty_FVar X
  | Ty_Arrow T1 T2 => Ty_Arrow (lift_ty T1) (lift_ty T2)
  | Ty_All T1 => Ty_All (lift_ty T1)   (* under its own binder the shift is the same: free bvars +1 *)
  | Ty_Int => Ty_Int
  end.
Note lift_ty is correct: shifting free bvars by 1 at any depth: under Ty_All, the bvar indices inside are relative to one more binder; free vars are those ≥ 1; shifting all by 1 maps free to free+1 ✓ and the bound var 0 stays 0? Fixpoint lift_ty_at (c : nat) (T : ty) : ty :=
  match T with
  | Ty_BVar i => if i <? c then Ty_BVar i else Ty_BVar (S i)
  | Ty_All T1 => Ty_All (lift_ty_at (S c) T1)
  ...
Then lift_ty = lift_ty_at 0.

Fixpoint subst_ty (envT : nat -> ty) (dT : nat) (T : ty) : ty :=
  match T with
  | Ty_BVar i => if Nat.ltb i dT then Ty_BVar i else envT (i - dT)

  | Ty_Arrow T1 T2 => Ty_Arrow (subst_ty envT dT T1) (subst_ty envT dT T2)
  | Ty_All T1 => Ty_All (subst_ty envT (S dT) T1)
  | Ty_Int => Ty_Int

Fixpoint subst_tm (envT : nat -> ty) (envM : nat -> tm) (dM dT : nat) (t : tm) : tm :=
  match t with
  | tm_bvar i => if Nat.ltb i dM then tm_bvar i else envM (i - dM)
  | tm_fvar x => tm_fvar x

Definitions:

Definition env_tm := nat -> tm.
Definition env_ty := nat -> ty.

Fixpoint subst_ty_d (env : env_ty) (d : nat) (T : ty) : ty :=
  match T with
  | Ty_BVar i => if Nat.ltb i d then Ty_BVar i else env (i - d)
  | Ty_FVar X => Ty_FVar X
  | Ty_Arrow T1 T2 => Ty_Arrow (subst_ty_d env d T1) (subst_ty_d env d T2)
  | Ty_All T1 => Ty_All (subst_ty_d env (S d) T1)
  | Ty_Int => Ty_Int
  end.

Fixpoint subst_tm_d (envT : env_ty) (envM : env_tm) (dM dT : nat) (t : tm) : tm :=
  match t with
  | tm_bvar i => if Nat.ltb i dM then tm_bvar i else envM (i - dM)
  | tm_fvar x => tm_fvar x
  | tm_abs T t1 => tm_abs (subst_ty_d envT dT T) (subst_tm_d envT envM (S dM) dT t1)
  | tm_app t1 t2 => tm_app (subst_tm_d envT envM dM dT t1) (subst_tm_d envT envM dM dT t2)
  | tm_tabs t1 => tm_tabs (subst_tm_d envT envM dM (S dT) t1)
  | tm_tapp t1 T => tm_tapp (subst_tm_d envT envM dM dT t1) (subst_ty_d envT dT T)
  | tm_int n => tm_int n
  | tm_div t1 t2 => tm_div (subst_tm_d envT envM dM dT t1) (subst_tm_d envT envM dM dT t2)
  | tm_arith op t1 t2 => tm_arith op (subst_tm_d envT envM dM dT t1) (subst_tm_d envT envM dM dT t2)
  end.

Fixpoint subst_q_d (envT : env_ty) (envM : env_tm) (dM dT : nat) (q : qualifier) : qualifier :=
  match q with
  | Pred_True => Pred_True
  ...
  | Pred_Eq t1 t2 => Pred_Eq (subst_tm_d envT envM dM dT t1) (subst_tm_d envT envM dM dT t2)
  ...
  end.

Lemma subst_tm_d_lc : forall t K k, lc_tm_at K k t -> forall envT envM dM dT, k <= dM -> K <= dT -> subst_tm_d envT envM dM dT t = t.

- tm_bvar i: i < k ≤ dM → subst leaves ✓.
- tm_fvar ✓.
- tm_abs T t1: lc gives lc_ty_at K T and lc_tm_at K (S k) t1; goal tm_abs (subst_ty envT dT T) (subst_tm envT envM (S dM) dT t1) = tm_abs T t1; f_equal; [subst_ty_d_lc with K ≤ dT | IH with S k ≤ S dM ✓].

Lemma subst_ty_d_open : forall T k U, locally_closed_ty U ->

  Note: after simpl, the LHS is subst_ty_d env d (if Nat.eqb (k+d) i then U else Ty_BVar i) — the opening index is k+d (open_ty_rec's parameter). Then destruct the eqb.

set_nth:
Fixpoint set_nth {A} (k : nat) (l : list A) (x : A) : list A :=
  match k, l with
  | O, l => x :: l        (* replaces position 0 even if empty *)
  | S k', [] => []        (* out of range *)
  | S k', a :: l' => a :: set_nth k' l' x
  end.
Then set_nth (S k) (a::l) x = a :: set_nth k l x ✓ definitional; set_nth 0 (a::l) x = x :: l ✓ definitional.
